proposal.hypothesis: Adding the seven selected static user-profile fields to w001 will improve official validation primary and its marginal portfolio contribution because their FM crosses create candidate-dependent personalization that is absent from the current hour+user-gap feature configuration.
proposal.implementation_plan: Apply the registry-owned selected_user_profile operator. In the features block, extend the current hour and strictly-earlier user-gap representation with the seven low-cardinality static pre-impression user profile fields. The trusted operator maps train-fitted categorical vocabularies to globally offset FM IDs and uses UNK for unseen evaluation values; the resulting fields interact with candidate video, author, duration bucket, hour, and user-gap fields through the existing FM.
proposal.justification: The proposed fields are legal at inference and can alter ordering within a user through interactions with candidate-item fields. The evidence studies the same incremental placement—on top of hour, exposure gap, and the watch-time auxiliary mechanism—making it more directly applicable than broad profile expansion or a new architecture family.
proposal.observation: The exact parent configuration contains only features ["hour","user_gap"] beyond its base representation, while the applicable catalog operator explicitly adds seven static pre-impression user fields. E002 reports that selected user-profile domains produced an incremental effect when added after hour, user-gap, and censored-watch auxiliary training.

research_evidence.query: Which legal context and side-information fields complement the FM?
research_evidence.reason: Broad side-feature additions can add noise; legal temporal context needs an explicit availability rule.
research_evidence.summary: Prioritize low-cardinality hour and train-derived user exposure-gap buckets before broad profile expansion. Compute all quantile edges from train only. The hour+user_gap BPR configuration reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604430330 ± 0.000459158; adding the censored watch-time auxiliary target reached 0.604607224 ± 0.000168363. Adding selected user profile domains on top reached 0.604821956 ± 0.000355822, a smaller incremental effect. The legal hour+gap+aux configuration also led the inspected random-exposure set at unbiased primary 0.378085981 ± 0.003012055. Any history feature must use train feedback or exposure-only information available at prediction time; evaluation-period long_view/play-time feedback is forbidden.

risk: Sparse profile-item crosses may overfit users or categories that drift after the train period.
The new member may be highly rank-correlated with w001 and therefore add little portfolio value.
UNK-heavy evaluation fields could reduce the effective representation gain.

evidence_adaptation.implementation_mapping: Primary block train: set HP['aux_weight']=0.2 and pass it through config['hp'] to SO.train; SO.train consumes the existing target produced for bpr_censored_watch and scales its censored-watch gradient relative to the BPR gradient. evidence_adaptation.protocol_caveat: E003 supports the mechanism and the 0.2 operating point relative to BPR alone, not necessarily superiority over this parent's 0.1 weight. Only the trusted fixed-split comparison can establish the incremental effect, and watch feedback remains train-only.
evidence_adaptation.source_mechanism: Keep native long_view pairwise ranking as the main objective while applying a small shared-embedding censored watch-time regression loss: exact residual for incomplete plays and a one-sided duration lower-bound hinge for completed plays.

proposal.hypothesis: Raising the connected censored watch-time auxiliary weight from 0.1 to 0.2 will improve the trusted primary and the refined member's marginal portfolio contribution by providing a stronger duration-aware training signal without replacing native long_view as the ranking objective.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit only the train block so HP['aux_weight'] changes from 0.1 to 0.2 before constructing the configuration passed to SO.train. Keep objective='bpr_censored_watch', all features, BPR settings, seeds, and checkpoint policy unchanged. The declared backend directly consumes aux_weight in the existing shared-FM censored-watch loss, whose incomplete-play term is an exact regression residual and whose completed-play term is a one-sided lower-bound hinge.
proposal.justification: The parent already contains the exact auxiliary mechanism, so changing only its consumed weight isolates signal strength rather than confounding target construction, architecture, and representation. The 0.2 setting is research-derived, but its benefit over the current 0.1 setting remains a falsifiable question for the official evaluator.
proposal.observation: The current connected training configuration uses objective='bpr_censored_watch' with hp.aux_weight=0.1. E003 identifies auxiliary weight 0.2 for a shared-embedding censored watch-time head and reports that this mechanism outperformed BPR without the auxiliary head under its evaluated protocols.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

risk: The current 0.1 coefficient may already be closer to the optimum, so 0.2 can overemphasize duration and reduce binary ranking quality.
The refined model may remain too correlated with w001 to improve the portfolio materially.
Noisy or censored watch-time gradients may increase seed variance.

proposal.hypothesis: Using eight sampled negatives per positive rather than four will improve official validation primary and marginal portfolio value by exposing each user embedding to a broader set of candidate-item comparisons during the same three training epochs.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit only the train block to set HP['n_neg']=8 instead of 4 before passing config to SO.train. Keep the data view, feature matrix, target, learning rate, batch size, epochs, regularization, embedding dimension, and auxiliary weight fixed. This is a connected configuration-only experiment because the trusted train_api explicitly lists n_neg as a supported key consumed by SO.train's BPR sampler.
proposal.justification: Doubling a sampler parameter that is demonstrably connected tests a bounded optimization hypothesis without introducing an inert key or changing the model family. More sampled comparisons may reduce pairwise-gradient variance and improve candidate discrimination, although the transition from four to eight has no supplied empirical guarantee.
proposal.mechanism: higher negative multiplicity for BPR sampling
proposal.observation: The parent uses n_neg=4 and only three epochs. The trusted runtime contract explicitly declares n_neg among the hp keys consumed by SO.train, whereas E001 shows that unrelated pair_group_weight keys were ignored and produced byte-identical predictions.

research_evidence.query: Which optimizer-side proposal failed because its configuration was not connected to the training backend?
research_evidence.reason: Prevent a later Agent iteration from repeating an executable-looking but semantically inert config-only patch.
research_evidence.summary: Deprioritize the exact tab inverse-frequency BPR proposal that only adds hp['pair_group_weight']='tab_invfreq' and hp['pair_group_weight_values'] before calling SO.train. In the locked formal run, all three seed predictions were byte-identical to the Legal parent because stable_ops did not consume either key. Before proposing any config-only optimizer change, trace the key to a concrete sampler, loss, or gradient consumer in current code; if no consumer exists within the allowed patch scope, reject the proposal rather than relying on static/smoke success. This is an implementation-specific no-op, not evidence that correctly wired group weighting can never work.

proposal.research_nonuse_reason: No supplied research record evaluates the specific connected transition from four to eight BPR negatives on this parent. E001 only diagnoses an inert unsupported weighting configuration, while E002 and E003 concern representation and auxiliary reward mechanisms. The explicit current backend contract is therefore the direct basis.
risk: Approximately doubling negative comparisons can increase runtime substantially.
Additional easy negatives may dilute useful gradients rather than improve them.
Keeping learning rate and epochs fixed may make the changed gradient mixture suboptimal.
The resulting ordering may be too correlated with w001 to add portfolio value.

rejected: Raising the connected censored watch-time auxiliary weight from 0.1 to 0.2 will improve the trusted primary and the refined member's marginal portfolio contribution by providing a stronger duration-aware training signal without replacing native long_view as the ranking objective.

Using eight sampled negatives per positive rather than four will improve official validation primary and marginal portfolio value by exposing each user embedding to a broader set of candidate-item comparisons during the same three training epochs.
selection_rationale: Candidate 0 has the strongest expected reliability-weighted marginal portfolio gain: it uses a registry-owned, connected feature operator, adds legal candidate-dependent FM interactions absent from w001, and E002 directly supports this representation at the same incremental placement above hour, user-gap, and censored-watch training. Its distinct personalization mechanism also offers more portfolio diversification than either scalar training refinement. Candidate 1 is connected, cheap, and well isolated, but E003 supports auxiliary weight 0.2 only versus BPR without the auxiliary head—not the proposed 0.1-to-0.2 transition—and the resulting member is likely highly correlated with w001. Candidate 2 is also connected and falsifiable, but the 4-to-8 negative transition has no positive empirical evidence, costs more, may add mostly easy negatives, and is likewise unlikely to diversify the portfolio. Therefore Candidate 0 best combines expected valid-primary gain, evidential and implementation reliability, and marginal portfolio potential.
